cards.explanation: The answer is "Do you speak Greek?" The commander hears a chained man ask politely for a word, and out comes that question (Acts 21:37). I think he was surprised, because he had a different man in mind. Paul gets his turn to talk anyway, friends.

Paul says he is a Jew from Tarsus. His words are, "I am a Jew from Tarsus in Cilicia, a citizen of no ordinary city." (Acts 21:39). One sentence and he's clearly not the Egyptian rebel. Short, true and to the point, friends.
The answer is True. Paul says, "Now I beg you to allow me to speak to the people." (Acts 21:39). A man in chains, asking for the mic. That's some nerve, friends, and I mean it as a compliment.

The answer is False. Paul motions to them and "A great hush came over the crowd…" (Acts 21:40). Picture a whole crowd going so quiet you could hear a cookie crumble. Quiet like that is worth noticing, friends.

The answer is Hebrew. Verse 40 says Paul "…addressed them in Hebrew…" The commander had asked him, "Do you speak Greek?" (Acts 21:37), and the crowd got Hebrew. And Acts 22:2 says that made them even quieter.

The answer is Gamaliel. Paul says, "I was educated at the feet of Gamaliel in strict conformity to the law of our fathers." (Acts 22:3). He also says he was raised in this city, and I bet that got the crowd's attention, friends.

The answer is a bright light from heaven. Paul says, "…suddenly a bright light from heaven flashed around me." (Acts 22:6). About noon, too, which is the brightest part of the day. A light that stands out at noon is not an ordinary light.

The answer is Jesus of Nazareth. The voice says, "I am Jesus of Nazareth, whom you are persecuting…" (Acts 22:8). Paul asked who it was, and he got a straight answer. I think that was a lot to take in on the ground, friends.

The answer is False. Paul says, "My companions saw the light, but they could not understand the voice of the One speaking to me." (Acts 22:9). They saw the light but could not understand the voice. I think that left them with a lot of questions.

The answer is True. Paul says, "…my companions led me by the hand into Damascus." (Acts 22:11). The brilliance of the light had blinded him. The man who planned to march in with letters had to be walked in by the hand, friends.

The answer is sight. Ananias says, "Brother Saul, receive your sight," and Paul says, "…at that moment I could see him." (Acts 22:13). The light had blinded him, and now he could see. Ananias called him brother, too, friends.
The answer is witness. Ananias says, "You will be His witness to everyone of what you have seen and heard." (Acts 22:15). A witness tells what he saw. And Paul had seen plenty, friends.

Ananias tells Paul to be baptized and wash his sins away. He says, "Get up, be baptized, and wash your sins away, calling on His name." (Acts 22:16). And he starts with "…what are you waiting for?" It sounds to me like a friend who has no time to waste.

The reason is that the people won't accept his testimony. The Lord says, "Hurry! Leave Jerusalem quickly, because the people here will not accept your testimony about Me." (Acts 22:18). Paul is telling this to the very crowd in Jerusalem. I think that makes this line hit hard, friends.

Paul says he watched over the garments of those who killed Stephen. His words are, "…I stood there giving my approval and watching over the garments of those who killed him." (Acts 22:20). He doesn't dress it up. He names exactly what he did, and that takes honesty, friends.
The answer is Gentiles. The Lord says, "Go! I will send you far away to the Gentiles." (Acts 22:21). Gentiles are people who aren't Jewish. And this is the very line the crowd couldn't take, friends.

They shout that he is not fit to live, and it's a hard one. They shout, "Rid the earth of him! He is not fit to live!" (Acts 22:22). I think this part hurts to read. Paul went from a hushed crowd to a roaring one in a single sentence, friends.

The commander orders that Paul be flogged and questioned. The text says he "…directed that Paul be flogged and interrogated…" (Acts 22:24). A flogging is a hard thing to read about, and I think it's heavy. Paul's about to say something that changes everything, though.

The answer is True. The commander wanted to "…determine the reason for this outcry against him." (Acts 22:24). The crowd was shouting, and he wanted to know why. His method was a hard one, though, friends.

The answer is citizen. Paul asks, "Is it lawful for you to flog a Roman citizen without a trial?" (Acts 22:25). He asks it while they're stretching him out to strap him down. Perfect timing for a question like that, friends.

The answer is False. The commander asks, "Tell me, are you a Roman citizen?" and Paul answers, "Yes" (Acts 22:27). One word, and the whole room changes. Then the commander says he paid a high price for his citizenship, and Paul tells him, "But I was born a citizen…" (Acts 22:28).
Paul was born a citizen. He says, "But I was born a citizen…" (Acts 22:28). The commander paid a high price for his, and Paul's came with his birth. I think that's a mic drop, if I may, friends.

The answer is alarmed. The text says "…the commander himself was alarmed when he realized that he had put a Roman citizen in chains." (Acts 22:29). He had chained a citizen. I bet his stomach dropped, friends.
